import pandas as pd, json
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

print(df[df.instance_family.isin(new_if)].date.min())
# confirm no other column values are new (e.g. new application names)

    print(c, 'new values:', set(post[c])-set(pre[c]))
res = [{"name": n, "type": "Instance Family"} for n in new_if]
json.dump(res, open('answer.json','w'))

Since a resource should be identified at the most meaningful level, let me check the hierarchy: the new applications are each a grouping of new instance families. The question asks for resource name = exact value in data.csv and type = the column. The most direct per-resource granularity is `instance_family` (125 rows), but new `application` values (20) also represent newly created resources. Let me examine which level best explains it — checking whether new instance families are uniquely tied to new applications.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
pre = df[df.date<'2025-09-20']; post = df[df.date>='2025-09-20']
new_apps = set(post.application)-set(pre.application)
print(sorted(new_apps))
# Are new apps composed ONLY of new instance families?
na = post[post.application.isin(new_apps)]
pre_if = set(pre.instance_family)
print('rows in new apps:', len(na), 'distinct IF:', na.instance_family.nunique(), 'all new IF?', set(na.instance_family).isdisjoint(pre_if))
# total cost from new apps on 9/20
print('new app cost 9/20:', na[na.date=='2025-09-20'].unblended_cost.sum())
# any pre-existing application with new instance families?
old_apps_post = post[~post.application.isin(new_apps)]
print('new IF in old apps:', set(old_apps_post.instance_family)-pre_if)
# per app costs pre-existing (for reference of app size)
print(pre.groupby('application').unblended_cost.sum().describe())
print(na.groupby('application').unblended_cost.sum().describe())
# check date coverage of new apps
print(na.date.min(), na.date.max())
print(na.groupby('application')['instance_family'].nunique())
